title: Your EV Can Power Your HOUSE. Here's How 🏠⚡ #shorts

scenes.text: Some electric cars hide a power plant. They can run your house.
Hyundai's Ioniq 5 has a normal outlet under the back seat, good for up to three point six kilowatts.
Electronics flip the battery's direct current into the AC your appliances use.
Ford's F one-fifty Lightning can push up to nine point six kilowatts into a home, from a pack of about one hundred thirty-one kilowatt-hours.
A typical home uses about thirty a day. That's roughly three days of backup, or up to ten if you ration.
It needs a bidirectional charger, and a switch that cuts your house off the grid to protect line crews.
So is the next power plant parked in your driveway? Follow EV Drive.
